"Dying 2? I've got a Hero Point. I've got plans."

Your Pathfinder Character Builder character, ready for the table: take damage and heal, go down and roll recovery checks, spend Hero Points, track conditions with their values, tick off spell slots and Focus Points, then rest and prepare. Click any skill, save, or Strike to roll it, at every multiple attack penalty.

The play sheet uses the characters saved by the Pathfinder Character Builder in this browser, apart from your D&D characters. Hit Points, conditions, slots, and the rest are saved with the character as you go, so they're still there after a reload, in an export, and in the Privacy page backup. Rolls go into the same history as the 🎲 dice button and the Dice Roller. A character in the party (👥 Add to Party) also shows its Hit Points and conditions on the Party Tracker and in the Initiative tracker, live, when they're open in this same browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Rules for dying, conditions, Hero Points, and rest are from Pathfinder Player Core by Paizo Inc., used under the ORC License.

How to use a Pathfinder 2e character sheet at the table

Build the character once in the Character Builder, then open it here (the ▶️ Play Sheet button on its sheet) for the session. The builder does the math; the play sheet keeps track of what changes from turn to turn.

Hit Points, dying, and wounded

  • Type an amount, then Damage, Heal, or Temp HP. Damage takes temporary Hit Points first, and temporary Hit Points don't stack: the higher amount stays.
  • At 0 Hit Points you're knocked out: unconscious and dying 1, or dying 2 if a critical hit did it (use From a Crit), plus your wounded value. Damage while dying adds 1 more (2 from a critical hit). Damage of double your maximum in one blow kills outright.
  • Roll the recovery check at the start of each turn: a flat check against DC 10 + your dying value. A success lowers dying by 1 and a critical success by 2; a failure raises it by 1 and a critical failure by 2. At dying 0 you're stable, and wounded goes up by 1. You die at dying 4, or sooner if you're doomed.
  • Healing brings you back from dying, and also adds 1 to wounded. Wounded ends when someone Treats your Wounds or you rest 10 minutes at full Hit Points: lower it by hand then.

Hero Points

Each session starts you at 1 Hero Point (⭐ New Session), and the GM hands out more, up to 3. Spend one to reroll a check: the ⭐ Reroll button in the roll bar rolls the last check again and keeps the new result. Spend all of them while dying for Heroic Recovery: no longer dying, stable at 0 Hit Points, and wounded doesn't go up.

Conditions and their values

Tap a condition to mark it and read what it does; frightened, sickened, clumsy, enfeebled, drained, stupefied, slowed, stunned, dying, wounded, and doomed carry a value you raise and lower with − and +. The sheet takes their penalties off your numbers for you: frightened and sickened on every check and DC, clumsy on Dexterity rolls and AC, enfeebled on Strength rolls and melee damage, drained on Fortitude (and your maximum Hit Points), stupefied on mental rolls and spells, fatigued on AC and saves, off-guard on AC, prone on attacks. Only the worst status penalty counts, and the worst circumstance penalty. End Turn lowers frightened by 1.

Spells, focus, and rest

  • Spontaneous casters tick off slots by rank; prepared casters tick off each prepared spell as they cast it. A cleric's divine font has its own row.
  • Focus spells spend Focus Points; Refocus (10 minutes) brings one back.
  • Rest & Daily Preparations (tap twice) is a full night's rest: Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier (at least 1) × your level, drained and doomed down by 1, fatigued gone, and every slot, Focus Point, and daily counter back.
  • Counters track anything else with uses: an alchemist's infused reagents, a staff's charges, a once-per-day feat or item.

Rolling from the sheet

Click Perception for initiative, a save, a skill, a Lore, or a Strike. Each Strike has three buttons: your first attack, then the second and third with the multiple attack penalty (−5 and −10, or −4 and −8 with an agile weapon). Crit doubles the damage and adds deadly and fatal dice. Fortune and Misfortune roll twice and keep the higher or lower until you switch back to Normal.

Works with

Edit the character or level up in the Character Builder, pick spells in the Spell Planner, check boosts with the Boost Calculator, and work out hit chances with the Attack Calculator.
